text:
anya: Quick sync — sketching a protocol UX that ties rollout flags, routing, and quota propagation into the edge layer. TL;DR: keep client-friendly REST while surfacing rollout+variant decisions to internal gRPC services via headers/metadata.

sam: ok curious. goal is to avoid changing all clients, right?

anya: yep. clients -> REST JSON at edge. Edge does: auth, quota claim, rollout decision, then transcodes to gRPC for internal services.

hannah: main risk I see is losing fidelity for typed protos (big structs) when transcoding. also metrics correlation.

raj: +1. we need consistent trace ids and a single quota token that follows the request through fanout. otherwise costing is a mess.

anya: agree. proposal: edge emits headers: `x-rw-rollout: v2-canary`, `x-rw-quota: qtok-<id>`, `x-rw-model-route: ml-variant-a`. These map to gRPC metadata on the other side.

pm-elena: from product POV: must be able to toggle rollout bucket per-route via Console and see per-bucket latency + errors in dashboards.

anya: right — Console will call control-plane to update rollout rules. Edge reads rules and adds `x-rw-rollout` per request. We tag metrics with rollout label.

sam: what about clients that expect long-poll or streaming? transcoding streams to gRPC bidi is hairy.

anya: streaming will be passthrough where possible (http2/gRPC), otherwise fallback to chunked responses with a thin adapter. We only transcode for unary requests.

raj: quota model: edge does optimistic reservation by calling Quota API with `client_id` + `route` and gets back `qtok`. Downstream services accept `qtok` and decrement locally when they commit. If qtok missing, reject.

hannah: can you show short example header mapping?

anya: sure:

```
# REST request from client
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json
{x: "prompt"}

# Edge adds headers
x-rw-rollout: v2-canary
x-rw-quota: qtok-4821
x-rw-model-route: llama-3-q8
traceparent: 00-...
```

```
# gRPC metadata received by service (pseudocode)
metadata["x-rw-rollout"] = "v2-canary"
metadata["x-rw-quota"] = "qtok-4821"
metadata["x-rw-model-route"] = "llama-3-q8"
```

raj: nice. For telemetry: we should add `rollout` as a label on all spans and metrics, and ensure sampling preserves one example per minute per bucket to guard SLOs.

pm-elena: and Console needs a per-rollout quick view: traffic %, p50/p95 latency, error rate, token cost.

hannah: does this force us to maintain multiple proto versions? if edge reuses JSON shapes it may hide proto-evolution problems.

anya: good call. edge should validate JSON against the canonical proto schema (server-side JSON->proto validation) and emit a `validation:fail` metric that triggers alerts if mismatches exceed threshold. That keeps backwards compatibility checks.

sam: how about the gateway pattern: single expressive gateway or lightweight translator sidecar for each service?

raj: I'm leaning to single edge for auth/quota/rollout + per-service sidecars for fast local decisions (cache of rollout rules). Edge does authoritative decision when it can. Sidecars fallback to local cached rules for retries/bypass.

hannah: can we avoid double billing when edge reserves quota and downstream also reserves? need an idempotent commit scheme.

anya: plan: qtok is a reservation token minted by quota service with TTL. Downstream must call quota commit API with qtok to finalize consumption. If commit fails, downstream should rollback local changes and return 429 or 500 so we don't double-charge.

pm-elena: how will we roll this out? phased?

anya: rollout plan:
- Phase 0: edge-only feature flag to add headers for a small % of traffic (read-only, no quota enforcement)
- Phase 1: enable optimistic quota reservation for canary routes (backend honors qtok but still fallback to legacy path)
- Phase 2: enforce qtok on all routes, sidecar caching enabled
- Phase 3: deprecate legacy adapters and flip streaming passthrough to gRPC-first where supported

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for `edge-rollout-protoux` on zone us-west-2 (build 2026.3.14-235) :rocket:

sam: what about error modes? if quota svc is down, edge should fallback to rate-limiting with token bucket and mark rollout=fail-open metric.

raj: agree — fail-open conservative throttling, but surface incidents to incidents channel and auto-disable canary assignment if errors spike.

hannah: are we logging payloads anywhere? keep PII out. Need clear redaction rules when we validate JSON against protos.

anya: yes — validation logs redact prompt and sensitive fields, only keep schema diffs. Retain hashes for debug.

pm-elena: summary: console shows rollout toggles, metrics per bucket, ability to abort and reassign. infra builds header mapping + qtok flow. eng-platform owners: who takes edge work?

sam: I can take edge mapping and quotas. raj will own quota commit flow. hannah will add proto-validation and metrics + alerts. anya will wire Console controls with control-plane.

anya: thanks team. I'll open RFC with the diagram + stub configs. short follow-up: anyone object to the header names? `x-rw-*` seems fine?

raj: fine. maybe `x-rw-quota-token` is clearer than `x-rw-quota`.

hannah: prefer `x-rw-rollout-id` vs `x-rw-rollout` for clarity.

anya: noted. will update RFC.

infra-bot: Created RFC rfc/edge-protocol-ux-328765. Link: https://r/edge-protocol-ux-328765

sam: cool. sync on Thursday?

anya: yep — 11am PT. short agenda: header mapping, qtok lifecycle, console UX.

pm-elena: thanks, meeting booked. :calendar:
